_comment: EXAMPLE allowlist-primary profile (ROADMAP R7) - adapt the allow list to your repo; NOT turnkey. defaultMode 'dontAsk' auto-denies anything not in permissions.allow. What the Read(.env*) deny actually covers: Claude's own file tools AND the file commands Claude Code recognizes inside a shell command (cat, head, tail, sed, grep), so `cat .env` IS refused. What it does not cover is a subprocess that opens the file itself - `python -c "print(open('.env').read())"`, `node -e ...`, an interpreter buried in a build script. That residual gap is closed one layer down by sandbox.filesystem.denyRead below, which is enforced for every child process, not just Claude's tools - which is why ./.env, ./.env.* and ./secrets appear there as well as in permissions.deny. Keep the hygiene rules anyway (do not commit real secrets; inject them from the environment or a secret manager): the sandbox is a per-session control, not a property of the repository. See managed/README.md 'Allowlist-primary profile (R7)'. Verified against code.claude.com 2026-08-12.

permissions._comment_deny: The Bash()/PowerShell() entries are not redundant under defaultMode 'dontAsk'. Deny is evaluated before allow, and the allow list above hands out whole command families - `Bash(git add:*)` would otherwise reach .claude/settings.json, and Read(./**)/Edit(./**) cover the baseline's own files. They match the command TEXT wherever the path appears, so they do not survive a `cd .claude` first or a path built from a variable; command-guard's tamper rule is the other half. The PowerShell command floor from settings.template.json (Remove-Item, Invoke-WebRequest, ...) is deliberately absent here: under 'dontAsk' every PowerShell command is denied unless it is in the allow list, so an enumerated deny would add nothing.

_comment_sandbox: Two things about this block are easy to get wrong. (1) SCOPE: strictAllowlist is honored from user settings, managed settings, or a CLI --settings file ONLY. In a repository's own .claude/settings.json it has no effect, so deploying this profile per-repo leaves the network allowlist in PROMPT mode - allowedDomains merely pre-approves the listed hosts, and an unlisted host asks instead of failing. Deploy this file through MDM/managed settings (or the org-wide allowManagedDomainsOnly) if you need egress to be a block rather than a question. (2) PATH FORM: './' or no prefix is relative to the project root for project settings - the '//' absolute-path convention belongs to permission rules, not to the sandbox. Note also what the sandbox does not reach: it governs Bash/PowerShell subprocesses, so the WebFetch tool is not sandbox-governed. Domains from WebFetch(domain:...) ALLOW rules do, however, join allowedDomains in the same allowlist strictAllowlist enforces.

filesystem._comment_denyRead: sandbox.filesystem.denyRead/denyWrite are enforced by the OS against child processes, so unlike a Read() permission deny they DO bound `python -c "open('.env').read()"` and similar subprocess reads. They are omitted here on purpose: this file is deployed as MANAGED settings, which have no project root, and project-relative './' paths are not supported at this scope. Add absolute paths (or '~/'-anchored ones) for the checkouts you actually deploy to.
